Write the Results to an Excel Workbook

Source: R/write_survival_workbook.R
write_survival_workbook.Rd

Writes the tables of the analysis to an Excel workbook (with the writexl package), one table per sheet with bold column names, with unrounded numbers (empty cells for missing values) and the print-ready names of the models (for example "Log-logistic" or "Hazards, 2 knots"). The sheets are:

Settings

Time unit, confidence level, reporting times and the versions of R and of the packages.

Data summary

summarise_data.

KM table

km_table at interval.

Hazard ratios, PH test

hazard_ratios and test_proportional_hazards (two or more arms).

Model status

Each model with its status ("ok", "warning" or "error") and message.

Fit statistics

gof_table.

Parameters

Parameters on the natural scale, with the rows of their variance-covariance matrix in the columns cov_1, cov_2, ... (column k is the covariance with the k-th parameter of the model).

Parameters (transformed)

The same on the scale on which the parameters are estimated (for probabilistic sensitivity analysis).

Covariance, Cholesky

covariance_table on both scales.

Survival summary

survival_summary with the restricted mean up to time_horizon.

Landmark survival

predict_survival at 0, interval, 2 * interval, ... up to time_horizon and at the landmark times.

Spline knots

spline_knot_table (spline models only).

Usage

write_survival_workbook(
  x,
  file,
  interval = NULL,
  landmarks = NULL,
  time_horizon = NULL,
  hazard_ratios = NULL,
  conf_int = TRUE,
  n_sim = 1000,
  seed = 1
)

Arguments

x

Object returned by fit_survival_models.

file

Path of the .xlsx file to write (replaced if it exists).

interval

Spacing of the reporting times of the Kaplan-Meier table and of the predictions. The default NULL uses the spacing of the time axis of the plots of the data (for example 12 months).

landmarks

Times at which the survival is predicted. The default NULL uses 6 months and 1, 2, 5 and 10 years, in the time unit of the data.

time_horizon

Time horizon of the predictions and of the restricted mean. The default NULL uses the last landmark time.

hazard_ratios

Data frame returned by estimate_hazard_ratio (for example with the covariates and strata chosen for the analysis). The default NULL uses the Cox model of the arm without adjustment.

conf_int

Logical; TRUE (the default) adds the simulated confidence intervals of the predictions and of the median, mean and restricted mean, which takes longer.

n_sim, seed

Number of simulations and seed of the confidence intervals (see predict_survival).

Value

The path file, invisibly.

Examples

dat <- processing_dataset(
  system.file("extdata", "fit_example.csv", package = "SurvFitSummary"),
  column_arm = "TRT01P", column_survtime = "AVAL", column_cnsr = "CNSR",
  control_arm = "Control"
)
fits <- fit_survival_models(dat, distributions = c("exp", "weibull"),
                            spline_scales = NULL)
path <- tempfile(fileext = ".xlsx")
write_survival_workbook(fits, path, conf_int = FALSE)
unlink(path)
